elements.element: If renewal does not require mutual written agreement, each automatic renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 provides that each Order Form automatically renews for twelve months.

elements.element: If renewal does not require mutual written agreement, Customer must be able to opt out of automatic renewal on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 permits either Party, including Customer, to prevent renewal by giving thirty days' advance written notice.

elements.element: If renewal does not require mutual written agreement, Vendor must remind Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the renewal date.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 expressly requires Vendor to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before the renewal date.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps recurring Fee increases at the lesser of the preceding twelve-month increase in CPI-U and three percent.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, the non-renewal notice window must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires thirty days' advance written notice, which is no more than sixty days.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 imposes the stricter cap of the lesser of CPI-U and three percent, and therefore cannot exceed five percent.

result.reason: The operative redline satisfies the preferred automatic-renewal alternative: twelve-month renewals, a 30-day Customer opt-out right, a Vendor reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% increase cap. It also satisfies the fallback. The edits are limited to shortening the existing notice period, clarifying its timing, and adding the required reminder; the existing renewal term and price provisions remain effective. Drafting quality is reduced because “gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end” is awkward and could be stated more precisely as “gives written notice at least thirty days before the end.”
